items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: It was a simple style. He got a nice tone, pretty tone. He could play. He was a good trumpet player.

ctx.x: Can you tell us anything about Paul Merez, how his tone was? I only heard him in the very late days of about 1938. I heard him play one or two Monday night sessions when they had him down at his barbecue place, and I don't remember too much about that. But was it a big tone or a simple style? What kind of a...
It was a simple style. He got a nice tone, pretty tone. He could play. He was a good trumpet player.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Well, Brunus and Paul Mraz, Rapolda, Ben Pollack, and El Meshogo, we all used to go down near Joe.

ctx.x: At Dreamland. How old were you then? About fourteen, thirteen, about fourteen. Did you know him by this time? Oh, yes. I knew him. You were speaking to him? Oh, yes. Sure. Was he nice to you? Very nice. Very nice. He thought it was wonderful that someone could try to play like him. Did you ever get together with him? Oh, yes. I was privileged to be one of the first white persons to sit in with Joe's band. Oh, yeah? Because he wouldn't let you sit in if you couldn't play. He didn't care who you were. Uh-huh. And…

What's where? You used to write that myth. Well, you used to the only song I know in that band. What band is that? They call it the rhythm case. It's called the rhythm case? Yeah. Myth mode? Yeah. No, myth didn't make it. I'm a myth.
